body:
## Goal
Implement the requested change from the agent mention.

## Original request
> I agree. This is the better customization boundary.
> 
> The current PR leans toward “Sepo defines a mini setup manifest.” After this discussion, I would instead frame the boundary as:
> 
> - Sepo provides a **small default hook** for common cases.
> - Repo owners can **edit the copied Sepo workflow** for complex cases.
> - Sepo docs should explicitly bless that workflow customization path instead of trying to model all of GitHub Actions inside `skill-setup.yaml`.
> 
> Concretely, I would change the PR direction like this.
> 
> 1. Replace `skill-setup.yaml` with an optional script convention:
> 
> ```text
> .skills/<name>/
>   SKILL.md
>   setup.sh      # optional
> ```
> 
> 2. Keep the workflow readable with a local action:
> 
> ```yaml
> - name: Run skill setup
>   uses: ./.github/actions/run-skill-setup
>   with:
>     skill: ${{ needs.portal.outputs.skill }}
>     skill_root: ${{ inputs.skill_root }}
>     trusted_ref: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/') }}
> ```
> 
> 3. Internally, that action only does simple things:
> 
> - resolve `<skill_root>/<skill>/SKILL.md`
> - check whether `setup.sh` exists
> - refuse PR checkout refs
> - run `bash <skill_dir>/setup.sh`
> - expose clear outputs/failure state
> 
> That lets us keep the useful path resolution/trust behavior from the current PR, but removes the custom YAML parser and the “is this becoming fake GitHub Actions?” concern currently centered in [`skills.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.agent/src/skills.ts#L193-L293).
> 
> 4. Add docs for advanced customization.
> 
> The docs should say: for complex skill routes, edit the copied `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` directly. The skill job already has a natural customization point after `Resolve skill package` and before `Run skill`: [`agent-router.yml#L419-L453`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/0d188a0ea041923b57657ebbf2ee045e80820de2/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L419-L453).
> 
> Example advanced customization:
> 
> ```yaml
> - name: Setup deep research skill
>   if: needs.portal.outputs.skill == 'deep-research'
>   uses: docker://ghcr.io/example/research-env:latest
>   with:
>     args: prepare-research-env
> ```
> 
> or:
> 
> ```yaml
> - name: Setup release skill
>   if: needs.portal.outputs.skill == 'release-notes'
>   uses: actions/setup-node@v4
>   with:
>     node-version: 22
> ```
> 
> That is much cleaner than making Sepo support Docker, `uses`, `with`, services, caches, matrix behavior, etc. Users already own the copied workflow, so advanced cases should use native Actions.
> 
> My recommended revision to PR #241:
> 
> 1. Remove `skill-setup.yaml` schema/executor.
> 2. Add optional `setup.sh` support.
> 3. Add `./.github/actions/run-skill-setup`.
> 4. Keep typed skill path resolution and PR-ref trust guard.
> 5. Update docs to explicitly define two levels:
>    - simple extension: `.skills/<name>/setup.sh`
>    - advanced extension: customize the `skill` job in `agent-router.yml`
> 
> That gives Sepo a minimal primitive without hiding the fact that larger customization belongs in the repo-owned workflow 

@sepo-agent /implement can we try to implement it in a new issue

## Acceptance criteria
- Implement the requested change.
- Preserve existing behavior unless the request requires a change.
- Update tests or validation as needed.

**Sepo implementation finished**

- Branch: `agent/implement-issue-250/codex-25975610901`
- Pull request: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/252

Added typed skill package resolution plus an optional `<skill_root>/<skill>/setup.sh` hook exposed through a new `./.github/actions/run-skill-setup` composite action, wired `skill_root` through skill prompt loading and the skill route, and documented the simple setup hook versus advanced workflow customization path. Verification: `npm --prefix .agent run build`, focused `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/skill-setup.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`, and `git diff --check` passed; full `npm --prefix .agent test` was attempted and only failed in existing onboarding CLI tests with local-runner `EPERM` writes to `_runner_file_commands`.
